text.p: Chubb Corp said Friday it was restating its preliminary 1996 financial results to reflect the classification of its life insurance business as a discontinued operation.
It said it was also taking the action to recognize a $160 million after-tax charge related to the write-down of certain real estate assets.
Last month Chubb reached a definitive agreement for Jefferson-Pilot Corp to purchase its Chubb Life Insurance Co of America unit for $875 million.
In addition to classyfing the unit as a discontinued oepation, Chubb said it was also recognizing an after-tax loss of $22 million on the sale.

Chubb also said that last month it decided to pursue the sale of certain real estate assets. It said it has since entered into an agreement with a prospective buyer to perform due diligence and anticipates executing a contract for the sale of substantially all of its commercial properties.
The change in strategy caused Chubb to reevaluate the carrying value of these assets, which resulted in the after-tax charge.

Taking into account the $160 million charge, it said its restated income from continuing operations for 1996 was $434.2 million. Income from continuing operations, including realized investment gains, was restated to $486.2 million.
Income from discontinued operations, was $26.5 million for 1996. Net income for 1996, restated, was $512.7 million or $2.90 a share.
